messages:
alex: Heads-up — we're planning a per-tier canary that only targets Premium + EU region. Need to decide routing/fallback priority when a variant is unavailable. API/console/telemetry implications?

maria: +1. Quick q: if premium users are pinned to a model version, should fallback respect the pin or the tier fallback?

joel: pin should win. Pinned version == tenant intent. If pinned is down, return an error rather than silently falling to cheaper model. Otherwise customers get inconsistent behavior.

alex: Agree on fail-fast for pins. For non-pinned tenants, we need a deterministic policy order we can document and show in console.

joel: Proposed order (simple): 1) explicit route override 2) tenant pin 3) per-tier variant 4) regional variant fallback 5) global default.

maria: That seems reasonable. Also need to clarify quota semantics — fallback to cheaper model must still consume the original tenant's quota tier, right? Premium shouldn't get charged at lower tier or vice-versa.

tina: Yes — keep billing semantics tied to customer tier. Implementation note: routing decision vs billing decision must be separate steps. Routing picks model, billing picks price_plan based on request.

alex: Agreed. Console UX: we should show a small 'scope matrix' on rollout page that lists exposure by tier/region and the fallback chain. Designers can show an expand/collapse where you can inspect "if variant X fails -> Y will be used".

maria: Telemetry wishlist: routing.fallback.count (labels: tier, region, from_variant, to_variant), routing.fallback.latency_p50/p95, rollout.exposure.{tier}.{region}.sample_rate. Also a trace link when fallback occurs.

joel: Add a circuit-breaker metric: routing.fallback.surge to detect cascading fallbacks. If we see > X fallbacks/min for a variant, auto-rollback canary for affected tiers.

alex: Good. For API change: I want a minimal change — add an optional `scope` field to rollout APIs, e.g. `scope: { tiers: ["premium"], regions: ["eu-west-1"] }`. If absent, applies global.

tina: API detail: what about partial overlap? e.g., scope tiers: ["premium"], regions: ["us-east-1", "eu-west-1"]. How are per-request decisions hashed? We should include a deterministic tie-breaker for multi-region tenants.

joel: Use request region first, then tenant tier. Hashing only used for sampling. For multi-region configs we evaluate region membership at routing time; if tenant reports region X use that bucket.

maria: UX: add per-tier sampling slider in console. Default to 5% for canaries on non-prod tiers, 0% for free. Need guardrails so someone can't accidentally expose 100% on premium.

alex: We should also decide whether fallbacks are counted as "errors" for rollout health. I think yes — fallback increases shown as fail rate on rollout page.

joel: +1. Implementation sketch (pseudoconfig):
```
{
  "rollout_id": "r-2026-005",
  "scope": {"tiers": ["premium"], "regions": ["eu-west-1"]},
  "variants": [{"model": "open-model-v2", "pct": 10}, {"model": "open-model-v1", "pct": 90}],
  "fallback_policy": ["tenant_pin","tier_variant","region_variant","global_default"]
}
```

maria: Nice. One more edge-case: dedicated customers (Dedicated clusters) should never fallback to hosted variants. That's a contractual thing. Need explicit enforcement in routing layer.

alex: Good catch. We'll add a top-level rule: if deployment_type == dedicated and requested_model not available -> reject (no fallback).

infra-bot: design doc created: https://redwood.internal/docs/routing/policy-priority — includes metrics, API examples, and circuit-breaker thresholds.

deploy-bot: FYI deploy started for a small test of scope field on staging (rollout-api v3).

maria: Next steps: I'll sketch console mockups, joel/tina can draft routing evaluation code + unit tests, alex will write spec and update docs.

alex: Awesome. Let's reconvene after the mock + design doc review. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
